basis: One advisory published to the GitHub Advisory Database 2026-09-30T23:53:17Z matching the pinned py:pyjwt@2.13.0, surfaced by hosted Foundation runtime run 36809316528 @de27290, which correctly failed closed (Restricted policy regressions: hosted-full-stack-dependency-audit, exit 1). Parsing the run's own check-run annotations (115 advisory ids) against the register and every earlier delta left exactly this one id uncovered. Reachability traced in the pinned source trees frappe@988e54f3c4c291e2077a83809663f123731abe76, erpnext@4048fb70e14d1843956fcdabb7c3cca75a1cbcdd, education@93bc7075753369457919720690f80c6d2207b5f2, payments@cca07d9f9392e2ea0e521c5975151db9e4b6c321 and hrms@a4768b441cff346def505e27f2a2229ee1e05b9b, plus the owned apps.

advisories.summary: PyJWT.decode() reintroduces options-dict mutation, enabling silent claim-verification bypass on dict reuse
advisories.runtime_disposition_evidence: The defect mutates a caller-supplied options mapping when verify_signature is falsy, so it only matters when application code reuses ONE options object across two or more jwt.decode()/decode_complete() calls (the advisory states calls that build a fresh options dict per call are unaffected; signature verification itself is unaffected). Repository-wide search of all five pinned upstream trees and the owned apps finds the complete jwt surface in frappe@988e54f3 only: frappe/oauth.py:324 jwt.encode (no options); frappe/oauth.py:446-454 jwt.decode with an inline literal options={verify_signature: False, verify_aud: False}; frappe/oauth.py:467-475 jwt.decode with a separate inline literal options={verify_exp: False}; frappe/utils/oauth.py:200 jwt.decode with an inline literal options={verify_signature: False}. Every call constructs its own dict at the call site; there is no module-level, class-level, instance-level or shared options object, so the mutated dict of the unverified-parse call is discarded and can never reach a verifying call (the second oauth.py decode already disables verify_exp explicitly and uses a different dict object). erpnext, education, payments, hrms and the owned apps (toefl_house, foundation_security) contain zero jwt imports or calls. PyJWT is a frappe dependency only (frappe/pyproject.toml: PyJWT~=2.13.0).
advisories.fix_path: Official Frappe release carrying a PyJWT release that contains the maintainers' prepared fix (no patched version published yet; EXTERNAL/UPSTREAM BLOCKED, unchanged posture)
